description: A binding typed with a *named* function type resolves to the node written in the alias, which every binding the alias types shares — so it can carry no key of its own without coloring all of them alike. What a consumer names is the binding, so that is what the chain is asked about, and the signature still supplies the facts. Both shapes: an interface member reached through a value, and a top-level `const` reached through an import.

diagnostics.message: Call to `paints.boom` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is colored `throwing` by the carrier that answers for it — a shipped manifest, an overlay, an override, or the standard-library baseline — so calling it can throw. Your outs, in precedence order: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@no-throw/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.
